summary: Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from ~1979 to 1984. She held a post at Rice University around 1990.

Helga Uebach was a scholar in Tibetology and Indology who completed her Ph.D. at the University of Munich (~1960–1967). In 1964, she served as a wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Hellfried Dahlmann worked in linguistics and held posts at the University of Marburg (~1935–1941) and the University of Cologne (~1941–1970).

Sinologist Hellmut Wilhelm earned his doctorate at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke. He taught German at Peking University (~1933–1948) and held the chair for Sinology at the University of Washington (1948–1971).

Hellmuth Hecker was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (1942–1948, PhD), where he also learned under Paul Debes in 1945. He served as a Referent at the University of Hamburg (~1952–1988).

Helmer Smith worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Uppsala University and under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He was a Dozent at Lund University (1921) and professor of Sanskrit at Uppsala University (1936–1947).

Helmut Eimer specialized in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Hamburg, Humboldt University, and Bonn (doctorate ~1968–1974) under Frank-Richard Hamm, later serving at the University of Bonn (~1974–2001).

Helmut Hoffmann specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earning degrees at Berlin under Heinrich Lüders and Marburg. He held posts at the Prussian Academy, Munich (1948–1968), the Bavarian Academy, and Indiana University Bloomington (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, completing his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He held posts at the University of Vienna, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and headed the IKGA (2007).

Linguist and Indologist Helmut Rix earned his PhD at Heidelberg and habilitation at Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen, Augustana-Hochschule Neuendettelsau, Regensburg, and was a professor at the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He held positions at the University of Vienna (attested 1983, 2010–2015 as professor, and 2026) and served as a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

Helmuth von Glasenapp was an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He held professorships at the University of Königsberg (1928–1944) and the University of Tübingen (1946–1959).

Sinologist and religious studies scholar Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer studied at the universities of Göttingen (~1967–1968) and Munich (~1968–1973). He held academic posts at the University of Munich (~1981–1993) and the University of Göttingen (~1993–2016).

Hemchandra Raychaudhuri was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Carmichael Professor and Head of the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta, attested in 1939 and 1965.
Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who held posts as professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 1991 and 2026.

Henepola Gunaratana is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his doctorate at American University. He served as principal of the Buddhist Institute of Kuala Lumpur and founded the Bhavana Society Forest Monastery and Meditation Center in 1985.

Heng Sure is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Ronald Y. Nakasone. He has held professorships at the Graduate Theological Union, Bond University, and Dharma Realm Buddhist University.

Henk Blezer is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who completed his education at Leiden University and CNWS. He held posts at CNWS, IIAS, and Leiden University, becoming University Lecturer in Buddhist Studies in 2008.

Indologist and linguist Henk Bodewitz completed his PhD at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He held the chair of Sanskrit at Utrecht University (1976–1992) and served as professor at Leiden University (1992–2002).

Henri Bergson was a philosopher who studied at École Normale Supérieure and the University of Paris. He taught at the lycée David d'Angers (~1881–1883) and held a post at the Collège de France (1900–1904).
